subject: Skyward AI — script handoff & allowlist checklist (post-demo)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@skywardai.com>, Priya Rao <priya@skywardai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Skyward AI — script handoff & allowlist checklist (post-demo)

Hi Jordan / Priya — great to meet you earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our perf/SLO qualification discussion so we can get the customer-led run scheduled: 

Recap from call:
- Target SLOs you confirmed: p95 generation latency < 200 ms (single-turn), sustained throughput target ~120 req/s for batch traffic, and up to 250 concurrent live streaming sessions with ~50 kb/s downstream per session.
- Primary test scope: 1) baseline throughput (non-streaming), 2) streaming concurrency ramp, 3) burst/steady-state p95 validation.
- Customer will run k6 scripts against a Redwood test endpoint during a 2-hour window; Redwood will provide allowlist IPs, a low-priv test account, and an initial k6 script to iterate on.

What we (Redwood) will provide by EOD tomorrow:
- initial k6 script (attached) tuned to your traffic mix + a short README with environment variables to point to our staging host.
- IP allowlist CSV and the exact source IP ranges for the run.
- ephemeral test account credentials and a per-test ingestion token (attached as a stub file).
- runbook checklist (quick items to confirm before start: tokens, metrics endpoints, tracing headers).

What we need from you by Thu, Dec 3:
- confirm test window (2-hour slot) and preferred start time (PST).
- confirm any additional geo-origin IPs we should include on the allowlist.
- provide any custom headers or auth flows used by your k6/Locust harness so we can ensure compatibility.

Proposed next step: schedule the run for Thu Dec 3, 10:00 AM PST. If that works, we'll lock the slot and send final run credentials and the allowlist.

Attachments: skyward_k6_script_v1.js (initial), allowlist_template.csv (blank).

Thanks — Rachel
Rachel Kim
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jordan Mills <jordan@skywardai.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@skywardai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyward AI — script handoff & allowlist checklist (post-demo)

Thanks Rachel — that recap looks right. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Throughput: 120 req/s is a good target; for the first run we'll do a 30-min steady-state at 120 req/s and then a 30-min step to 200 req/s to observe degradation behavior.
- Streaming: we can start the concurrency ramp to 250 over 20 minutes; payloads are small telemetry events (approx 2-3 KB per message).
- Auth: we use an API key header X-SWA-API-Key for non-streaming traffic and an ephemeral token in the WebSocket handshake for streaming. We'll provide exact header names if they differ.

Availability: Thu Dec 3, 10:00 AM PST works for our infra team.

One ask: please include an example k6 scenario that simulates the streaming handshake (we can emulate via http long-poll if needed) — otherwise our script team will adapt.

Jordan
Jordan Mills
Head of Platform Engineering | Skyward AI
jordan@skywardai.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@skywardai.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 10:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyward AI — script handoff & allowlist checklist (post-demo)

Hi Jordan — looping in a short technical note and the initial script attached.

Technical notes: 
- The attached file skyward_k6_script_v1.js includes three scenarios: baseline_http (120 req/s), throughput_step (120 -> 200 req/s), and streaming_probe (emulated via long-polling /chunked endpoint to approximate websocket behavior). We added a HEADERS block where you can set X-SWA-API-Key and any other custom headers.
- P95 measurement: Redwood's default telemetry will report p50/p95/p99 at 10s aggregation windows. We'll provide a shared Grafana dashboard link during the run.
- IP ranges: please confirm the following will be added to your allowlist so our orchestrator can send traffic from them: 35.201.12.0/24, 35.201.13.0/24, 34.82.45.0/24. (We'll provide a CSV version — attached allowlist_template.csv filled.)
- Test accounts: attached test-account-credentials.txt is a placeholder with a low-priv user and an ingestion token; we'll rotate the token after the run.

Safety and throttles: we'll enforce gradual ramping by default and watch for 5xx spikes — if we observe sustained 5xx > 1% we'll throttle and notify.

Please confirm the IP ranges and the streaming handshake token name (ephemeral token header) before Thu EOD so we can finalize the slot.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

[Attachment: skyward_k6_script_v1.js]
[Attachment: allowlist_template.csv]
[Attachment: test-account-credentials.txt]

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan@skywardai.com>, Priya Rao <priya@skywardai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyward AI — script handoff & allowlist checklist (post-demo)

Perfect — thanks all for the quick confirmations. Final checklist for Thu Dec 3, 10:00 AM PST:

- Redwood provides: filled allowlist CSV (attached), skyward_k6_script_v1.js, ephemeral test account + token, Grafana link and tracing headers.
- Skyward provides: confirmation that 35.201.12.0/24, 35.201.13.0/24, 34.82.45.0/24 are allowed, and the exact ephemeral token header name (Jordan noted this is used in the WS handshake).
- Run plan: 00:00-00:30 baseline at 120 req/s; 00:30-01:00 step to 200 req/s; 01:00-01:20 streaming ramp to 250 concurrent sessions over 20 minutes; 01:20-02:00 post-run cool-down / log collection.
- Success criteria: p95 <= 200 ms for single-turn baseline and p95 degradation profile documented for step run. If we hit >1% 5xx we'll stop and capture heap/trace data for analysis.

Jordan / Priya — confirming the slot now. Please reply-all with your allowlist confirmation and the streaming token header name (or we can read it from your test-auth doc).

See you Thu.

Rachel
